2. MFA No.200183/2023 is filed by the claimants i.e the legal heirs of deceased Mahadev, seeking enhancement of compensation.
Whereas, MFA No.202287/2023 is filed by the Corporation seeking reduction of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal and also to set aside the liability fixed on the Corporation.
Brief facts of the case are that, on 05.09.2021 the deceased in this case one Mahadev was proceeding towards the bridge in Sangavi village, Akkalkot taluka, District Solapur.
When he was near the bridge, at that time the driver of MSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.MH-14/BT- 0501 drove it with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit against the said Mahadev.

Due to which,
he sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

Hence, FIR was registered against the driver of MSRTC, in Crime No.433/2021 and thereafter the jurisdictional police investigated the matter and laid the charge sheet against him under the provisions of IPC and IMV Act.

A claim petition was filed by the legal heirs of deceased i.e. wife, three children and mother of the deceased Mahadev under Section 166 of the M.V.Act in MVC No.1330/2021 before the MACT, Kalaburagi.
The said claim petition was opposed by the Corporation on the ground that the deceased has committed suicide and it was not a case of accident.

On the basis of the pleadings and material on record, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 05.09.2021 the deceased Mahadev was proceeding by walk by the side of the road towards bridge of Sangavi village, at that time MSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.MH- The Divisional Controller Msrtc vs Anita Devkar And Ors on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177184446/
4 14/BT-0501 being driven by its driver came in high speed and in rash and negligent manner dashed to the Mahadev. Due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries over his head and died on the spot?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition from respondent?
3. What order or award?
5.
To prove the claim before the MACT, petitioner No.1 herself examined as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
On the other hand, driver of bus-respondent is examined as RW1 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.

After assessment of the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.31,02,800/- together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of amount and directed the respondent i.e. Corporation to deposit the said compensation.

7. The said judgment and award is challenged under these appeals by both the claimants so also the respondent-Corporation as stated supra.
8.

We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants in MFA No.200183/2023 so also the learned counsel for the Corporation/appellant in MFA No. 202287/2023.
9.

The learned counsel for the appellants in MFA No.200183/2023 would contend that the Tribunal erred in awarding the compensation which is on the lower side and the Tribunal failed to appreciate both the oral and NC: 2023:KHC-K:6553-DB documentary evidence.
The Tribunal erred in considering the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.14,250/-, though the deceased was an agricultural labour and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The Tribunal also failed to award proper compensation under the head of consortium and other heads.
Hence, he prays to allow the appeal and to enhance the compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Corporation would vehemently contend that the deceased Mahadev was standing beside the road and jumped in front of the moving bus and committed suicide.
Therefore, it is not a case of accidental death, rather a case of suicidal death.
Hence, the Corporation is not liable to pay compensation.
He would further contend that the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased on the higher side and the amount awarded under various heads are also on the higher side.
Hence, he prays to set aside the judgment and award.
We have bestowed our anxious consideration, to the submissions made by both the parties and also perused the materials available on record including the Trial Court records.

sentences.text: On careful perusal of the material available on record, it can be gathered that on 05.09.2021 the deceased Mahadev was proceeding by walk by the side of the road towards bridge of Sangavi village and at that time MSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.MH-14/BT-0501 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the said Mahadev.
Due to which, he fell down and sustained injuries.

Though this aspect was disputed by the learned counsel for the Corporation by urging that the deceased has committed suicide by jumping infront of the moving bus, however, a perusal of Ex.P1 the first information report and Ex.P3-charge sheet submitted by the jurisdictional police, clearly depicts that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
The jurisdictional police after - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6553-DB conducting detailed investigation in the matter has laid the charge sheet against the offending bus driver as per Ex.P3.
The Respondent/Corporation before the Trial Court failed to disprove the said aspect of the matter by leading cogent evidence.

Hence, we are of the considered view that the accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the MSRTC i.e. Corporation and the death of the deceased Mahadev was not suicidal one and accordingly the contention raised by the Corporation is liable to be rejected.

13. As far as the appeal filed by the claimants for enhancement of compensation is concerned, on careful perusal of the judgment passed by the Tribunal, it is seen that the Tribunal has meticulously examined the evidence and the documents produced by the claimants so also the respondent-Corporation and rightly awarded a total compensation of Rs.31,02,800/- on different heads.

The Tribunal rightly considered the income of the deceased and on applying proper multiplier, awarded compensation - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6553-DB towards loss of dependency so also on the head of consortium and towards funeral and loss of estate.
We find no good grounds to interfere with the said judgment and award and to enhance the compensation.
Hence, the appeal filed by the claimants is also liable to be rejected.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Both the appeals, MFA No.200183/2023 and MFA No.202287/2023 are dismissed.
